title: Residency Chronicle and Auto-Reporting for Scheduled Switchover Controls
creator: Alexandra Chen
description: Objective: implement a tamper-evident residency chronicle (append-only event stream) and an automated reporting pipeline for scheduled regional switchover operations in Private/VPC/on-prem deployments. This ticket covers: (1) schema for residency events (node location, NIC, zone, ip alloc, kube node id, timestamp, change-cause), (2) retention controls tied to customer tenancy and compliance policies, and (3) an evidence generation job that bundles signed chronicle slices and system artifacts for auditors when a scheduled switchover occurs. The feature must work for both planned (scheduled maintenance, capacity rebalancing) and policy-driven switchover (jurisdictional evacuation) while preventing accidental cross-region data egress.
acceptance_criteria: Residency chronicle event schema finalized and documented in Confluence with examples (create/terminate/move/metadata-change).
Chronicle is written as append-only objects to customer-owned S3 or on-prem artifact store, signed with KMS/HSM-backed keys, and immutable for the configured retention window.
Retention settings are configurable per-tenant via Console and default to customer policy; UI change gated behind RBAC and audit log entries recorded for every adjustment.

Automated evidence bundle generator runs post-switchover and produces a ZIP containing chronicle slice, node-level checksums, network ACL snapshots, service topology, and a machine-signed manifest. The bundle upload endpoint shows success/failure in Console activity feed.
End-to-end integration tests covering scheduled switchover path verify no external egress beyond allowed regions; tests added to nightly pipeline and dashboarded.

Performance: chronicle writes do not add >5ms p99 latency to control-plane operations under normal load, and artifact generation completes within SLA window (configurable, default 10m) for clusters up to 200 nodes.
Security review completed and SRE runbook for manual evidence extraction and emergency rollback is published.

technical_notes: Event format: newline-delimited JSON with base64 payload for binary blobs; include canonicalized fields to make signatures verifiable across regions.
Use envelope encryption: object encrypted with tenant key, signature produced by control-plane KMS (HSM-backed), and manifest signed by customer-managed key if provided.
Retention enforcement: control-plane retains pointer metadata beyond configured retention but revokes access token; physical deletion handled by tenant artifact store lifecycle when available.
For on-prem installs, provide an operator that writes chronicle to local immutable filesystem mount and rotates signed snapshots to customer KMS-backed HSM.
To avoid latency cliffs, writes are async by default with a synchronous checksum-on-success path for high-assurance customers (opt-in); default remains async to meet latency SLO.

risks: Potential for accidental synchronous writes to increase control-plane latency; mitigated by defaulting to async with opt-in sync mode.
Legal/regulatory differences across regions make one-size-fits-all retention defaults risky; require explicit per-tenant policy acceptance for defaults.
On-prem environments may not provide immutable storage guarantees; we will ship operator with best-effort immutability and document limitations.
Signing keys management adds operational complexity for customers; provide clear docs and automation for key rotation.
Evidence bundle size for large clusters could exceed upload windows; implement chunking and resumable uploads.
